subject: Clarify: MSA security appendix — evidence rotation and pen-test lifecycle
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morrison <security@acmehealth.com>, Samir Khan <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify: MSA security appendix — evidence rotation and pen-test lifecycle

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for pushing this through on your side. Per our last call, I attached a working draft of the security appendix we plan to include with the order form. Two quick items we want to confirm before Laura and I submit redlines:

1) Pen-test window and notification: We propose a 30-day advance notice for externally executed pen tests, with a mutually agreeable 5-business-day blackout window for critical change freezes. Can you confirm your preferred minimum notice and whether your security team needs a fixed calendar window (e.g., Q1) or flexible scheduling?

2) Evidence rotation / SOC 2 access: Redwood maintains a rolling SOC 2 report cadence and can share the latest report and summary of scope. For customer evidence requests (audit rights), we typically provide an evidence bundle on a 60-day cadence and a one-time live evidence review. Please confirm if Acme requires continuous evidence streaming / additional log extracts beyond the bundle.

Attachments: redwood_security_appendix_v1.docx (working draft), proposed-pen-test-window.xlsx (two schedule options), SOC2-scope-summary.pdf

High-level ask: If you can reply with the preference for notice period and whether you need recurring evidence exports or ad-hoc access, we’ll fold that into the MSA redline we send to legal.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

—
Logan Wright
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com | +1-415-555-0123

From: Elena Morrison <security@acmehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Khan <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: MSA security appendix — evidence rotation and pen-test lifecycle

Logan —

Thanks for the doc. Quick answers from our side:

- Pen-tests: We prefer 45 days' written notice for any external tests that include vulnerability scanning or credentials provided by us (this gives our environment team time to prepare and schedule maintenance windows). A 5-business-day blackout for emergency patches is fine and expected.

- Scheduling: Flexible scheduling is OK; we do not need a fixed quarter unless it's a production-impacting test. If you can provide two proposed 2-week windows (early and late), we can lock one in after procurement signs off.

- Evidence: Standard approach for us is a 30/90 hybrid: we ask for a current SOC 2 report and a 30-day snapshot of relevant logs for data-flow-related assertions, plus a 90-day evidence bundle for configuration/attestation artifacts. We do not require continuous streaming, but we do ask for a documented process to request ad-hoc extracts with a 5-business-day SLA for delivery.

I attached a short spreadsheet with our preferred windows and required artifacts for each evidence round.

If Laura has any legal constraints on notice windows, please flag now — we can be flexible on the formal notice period if Redwood has concerns.

Best,
Elena
Elena Morrison
Head of InfoSec | Acme Health
security@acmehealth.com

Attachment: acme_security_requirements.xlsx (summary of windows & artifacts)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morrison <security@acmehealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: MSA security appendix — evidence rotation and pen-test lifecycle

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the quick, clear feedback. A couple of legal points for negotiation so we can close the MSA + order form together:

1) Notice period: Acme's 45-day ask is reasonable; we typically accept 30–45 days. Please note our internal change freeze policy requires notice to our infra team and we cannot guarantee environment snapshots outside of agreed windows. We'll accept 45 days with the following carve-outs: (a) emergency remediation tests initiated by Acme require at least 10 business days' notice if they require access to customer-provided credentials, and (b) Redwood maintains the right to delay non-critical tests to avoid SLA violations for other customers in shared environments.

2) Audit rights & evidence scope: We need to narrow the evidence scope in the appendix to protect third-party customer data and platform confidentiality. Proposal: we will provide (i) SOC 2 Type II report, (ii) a redacted 30-day log extract limited to metadata (no PII), and (iii) a 90-day configuration snapshot for the bounded service footprint used by Acme. Any additional ad-hoc extracts will require a signed DPA addendum with specific fields identified.

3) Pen-test coordination: We ask that pen-tests that are vendor-executed and include credentialed access be run in a dedicated test environment whenever feasible. If executed against production, we require a testplan 10 business days prior so our ops team can triage risk.

Action items for Logan / Karthik: please incorporate the language above into the redline and flag any technical constraints that prevent us from meeting Acme's evidence expectations. Karthik — can you confirm if we can provide the requested 30-day metadata extract without exposing customer PII?

Thanks — I’ll prepare a tracked redline of the appendix once we have Karthik's confirmation.

—
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morrison <security@acmehealth.com>, Samir Khan <procurement@acmehealth.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: MSA security appendix — evidence rotation and pen-test lifecycle

Elena / Samir — thanks for the quick turnaround and Laura / Karthik for the legal/technical checks. Summary and next steps:

- Notice: We’ll accept the 45-day external pen-test notice. Redwood will add the emergency remediation clause (10 business days) and a provisioning note that we may defer non-critical tests to prevent cross-customer SLA impacts.

- Evidence: Redwood to provide SOC 2 Type II (most recent), a redacted 30-day metadata-only log extract, and a 90-day configuration snapshot. Any further extracts will require the DPA addendum. Karthik is actioned to confirm PII redaction feasibility by EOD Wednesday.

- Scheduling: Logan to propose two 2-week windows by EOD Wednesday; Acme to lock one after procurement sign-off.

- Deliverables: Laura to circulate the tracked redline of the security appendix by Thu (11/12). Logan to upload the redline and the two proposed pen-test windows to the shared Drive.

If no objections, I’ll convert the draft into a tracked redline and push to the HubSpot deal for formal approval.

Thanks —
Logan
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
